transcript: Last night, I saw Our Town on Broadway. This play is about a constellation of everyday characters and experiences in a small New Hampshire town in the early 20th century. It feels like a love letter to quaint, small town life and to the ordinary and the mundane. It stars Jim Parsons who is great in this. As the stage manager, he narrates and provides all kinds of background information on the town and the characters, interspersed with philosophies about life and love. He delivers his lines with a nice blend of earnestness and sarcasm, capturing how experiencing life both inspires us and jades us. Despite this being one of the very few well known plays that take place in New Hampshire, which is the state I grew up in, I actually had never seen or read it before. My understanding is that it's usually performed in two acts over two and a half hours, but this production is about 100 minutes with no intermission. I was really happy about that and I thought the pacing was great. Respectfully, I actually imagine that a two act version of this story could bore me. I found this production to be much like the town it's about: simple, wholesome, but not remarkably memorable except for maybe one sensory surprise toward the end. It’s marketed to be the “Our Town for our time” but it's not exactly clear to me what makes this production fit that bill other than it being short enough for our tiny 21st century attention spans. Nevertheless, this was a solid, enjoyable production. With that, another playbill for my collection.
